evals.prompt: Write the least-privilege IAM configuration for running an AWS FIS EC2/RDS experiment in `ap-south-1`: (1) the `FISExperimentRole` trust policy for `fis.amazonaws.com` with confused-deputy protection (`aws:SourceAccount` and `aws:SourceArn`), (2) the permissions policy restricting `ec2:StopInstances` / `ec2:StartInstances` to resources tagged `ChaosReady=true`, and (3) the operator's `iam:PassRole` policy statement restricted with `iam:PassedToService`.
evals.expected_output: Provides (1) the `fis.amazonaws.com` trust policy with `aws:SourceAccount` and `aws:SourceArn` (`arn:aws:fis:ap-south-1:<account_id>:experiment/*`), (2) the execution policy restricting mutating EC2/RDS actions via `aws:ResourceTag/ChaosReady: "true"`, and (3) the operator `iam:PassRole` statement conditioned on `iam:PassedToService: "fis.amazonaws.com"`.
expectations: Provides the `FISExperimentRole` trust policy for `Service: fis.amazonaws.com` containing both `aws:SourceAccount` and `aws:SourceArn` (`arn:aws:fis:ap-south-1:<account_id>:experiment/*`) conditions
Scopes the destructive action permissions (`ec2:StopInstances`, `ec2:StartInstances`) using a tag condition (`aws:ResourceTag/ChaosReady: "true"`)
Provides the operator's `iam:PassRole` policy statement scoped to the `FISExperimentRole` ARN with `Condition: {"StringEquals": {"iam:PassedToService": "fis.amazonaws.com"}}`

evals.prompt:
An engineer wrote a script with these 6 broken AWS FIS CLI commands and action IDs:
1. `aws fis create-experiment --cli-input-json file://template.json`
2. `aws fis start-experiment --template-id EXT12345`
3. `aws fis get-experiment --experiment-id EXP98765`
4. `aws fis stop-experiment --experiment-id EXP98765`
5. Action IDs `aws:iam:inject-api-error` and `aws:eks:terminate-pods`
6. Action ID `aws:rds:failover-db-instance` for a standard Multi-AZ RDS PostgreSQL instance
Correct all 6 errors with the exact AWS FIS CLI commands, flags, and action IDs.
evals.expected_output: Corrects all 6 items: (1) `aws fis create-experiment-template`, (2) `aws fis start-experiment --experiment-template-id EXT12345`, (3) `aws fis get-experiment --id EXP98765`, (4) `aws fis stop-experiment --id EXP98765`, (5) `aws:fis:inject-api-internal-error` / `aws:fis:inject-api-throttle-error` / `aws:fis:inject-api-unavailable-error` and `aws:eks:pod-delete`, and (6) `aws:rds:reboot-db-instances` (`forceFailover=true`) for standard RDS instances vs `aws:rds:failover-db-cluster` for Aurora clusters.
expectations: Corrects `create-experiment` to `aws fis create-experiment-template` and `--template-id` on `start-experiment` to `--experiment-template-id`
Corrects `--experiment-id` on `get-experiment` and `stop-experiment` to `--id` (while noting `list-experiment-resolved-targets` uses `--experiment-id`)

Corrects `aws:iam:inject-api-error` to `aws:fis:inject-api-internal-error` / `aws:fis:inject-api-throttle-error` / `aws:fis:inject-api-unavailable-error` and `aws:eks:terminate-pods` to `aws:eks:pod-delete`
Corrects `aws:rds:failover-db-instance` to `aws:rds:reboot-db-instances` (with `forceFailover: "true"`) for standard Multi-AZ RDS instances and `aws:rds:failover-db-cluster` for Aurora DB clusters

evals.prompt: /aws-resilience:chaos-experiment Check if any AWS Fault Injection Service (FIS) experiment templates currently exist in `ap-south-1` (read-only). Then design a complete FIS experiment template JSON that stops 50% of EC2 instances tagged `ChaosReady=true` in `ap-south-1a`, waits 5 minutes (`PT5M`) via `aws:fis:wait`, restarts them (`startInstancesAfterDuration`), logs with `logSchemaVersion: 2`, and aborts automatically if our CloudWatch alarm `High5XXErrorAlarm` fires.
evals.expected_output: Performs read-only discovery in `ap-south-1` (`list-experiment-templates`), provides the complete FIS template JSON with `aws:ec2:stop-instances` (`startInstancesAfterDuration: PT5M`), `aws:fis:wait` with mandatory `"targets": {}` and `startAfter`, `selectionMode: "PERCENT(50)"` with `resourceTags: {"ChaosReady": "true"}` and AZ filter, `stopConditions` with `source: "aws:cloudwatch:alarm"`, and `logConfiguration` with `logSchemaVersion: 2`.
expectations: Performs read-only discovery in `ap-south-1` checking existing FIS experiment templates (`list-experiment-templates`) and reports live findings honestly
Uses the exact action ID `aws:ec2:stop-instances` (plural) and chains the `aws:fis:wait` action with `duration: "PT5M"` and `startAfter`

Configures `selectionMode: "PERCENT(50)"` with `resourceTags` (`ChaosReady: true`) and warns that `PERCENT(n)` rounds down to the nearest integer (so 1 matching instance resolves to 0 targets and fails)
Includes a mandatory `stopConditions` entry with `source: "aws:cloudwatch:alarm"` and `logConfiguration` with `logSchemaVersion: 2`

evals.prompt: /aws-resilience:game-day-runbook Before injecting real faults during our GameDay in `ap-south-1`, how do we run a safe dry-run target preview in AWS FIS to verify the exact resource ARNs that our tag and AZ filters will match without executing any fault actions?
evals.expected_output: Explains setting `"experimentOptions": {"actionsMode": "skip-all"}` on the experiment template (or `--experiment-options actionsMode=skip-all` on `start-experiment`), running the preview experiment, and calling `aws fis list-experiment-resolved-targets --experiment-id <EXP_ID>` to inspect the resolved resource count and ARNs before running with `actionsMode=run-all`.
expectations: Specifies using `actionsMode: "skip-all"` in `experimentOptions` to resolve targets without executing any fault injection actions
Specifies calling `aws fis list-experiment-resolved-targets --experiment-id <experiment_id>` to verify the exact resolved resource ARNs and target counts before switching to `run-all`

evals.prompt: Why did `aws fis create-experiment-template` fail with `InvalidParameterException: logSchemaVersion` when we passed `"logSchemaVersion": 1` with `cloudWatchLogsConfiguration`, and what permissions are required when delivering FIS experiment logs to a KMS-encrypted CloudWatch Log Group or S3 bucket?
evals.expected_output: Explains that current FIS `logConfiguration` requires `"logSchemaVersion": 2`, and details the `FISExperimentRole` permissions (`logs:CreateLogDelivery`, `logs:PutResourcePolicy`, `logs:DescribeResourcePolicies`, `logs:DescribeLogGroups` for CloudWatch Logs; `s3:PutObject`, `s3:GetEncryptionConfiguration` + `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:Decrypt` for SSE-KMS S3 buckets).
expectations: States that `logSchemaVersion` in `logConfiguration` must be set to integer `2` (`"logSchemaVersion": 2`)

Lists the required `logs:CreateLogDelivery`, `logs:PutResourcePolicy`, `logs:DescribeResourcePolicies`, and `logs:DescribeLogGroups` permissions on the FIS IAM role (plus `kms:GenerateDataKey` / `kms:Decrypt` for KMS-encrypted destinations)

evals.prompt: We granted `FISExperimentRole` full `eks:*` and `ec2:*` IAM permissions in `ap-south-1`, yet our `aws:eks:pod-delete` and `aws:eks:pod-network-latency` FIS experiment fails immediately with `Unauthorized` / `Forbidden` when trying to target pods in namespace `payments`. Why are AWS IAM permissions alone insufficient for EKS FIS actions, and what Kubernetes RBAC and EKS Access Entry configuration is required?
evals.expected_output: Explains the EKS RBAC trap: `FISExperimentRole` authenticates to the Kubernetes API server inside the EKS cluster, so in addition to AWS IAM permissions it must be mapped into the EKS cluster (via an EKS Access Entry or `aws-auth` ConfigMap) and bound via a Kubernetes `Role` + `RoleBinding` in namespace `payments` granting `get`, `list`, `delete` on `pods` (and `pods/exec` / `jobs` for network fault injection).
expectations: Explains that AWS IAM permissions (`eks:*`) only cover the AWS control plane, whereas `aws:eks:pod-delete` and `aws:eks:pod-network-*` interact directly with the Kubernetes API server inside the cluster
Specifies mapping `FISExperimentRole` into the EKS cluster via an EKS Access Entry (`aws eks create-access-entry`) or `aws-auth` ConfigMap
Provides the Kubernetes `Role` and `RoleBinding` in the target namespace (`payments`) granting permissions on `pods` (`get`, `list`, `delete`, and pod/job creation for network faults)

evals.prompt: How do we configure an AWS FIS experiment using `aws:ssm:send-command` with the managed document `AWSFIS-Run-CPU-Stress` (or `AWSFIS-Run-Memory-Stress`) on EC2 instances in `ap-south-1`, how are `documentParameters` formatted in the FIS action JSON, and why does the action fail if instances are in a private subnet without SSM endpoints?
evals.expected_output: Shows the `aws:ssm:send-command` action with `documentArn: "arn:aws:ssm:ap-south-1::document/AWSFIS-Run-CPU-Stress"`, `documentParameters` as a serialized JSON string (`"{\"DurationSeconds\":\"120\",\"CPU\":\"0\"}"`), `duration: "PT2M"`, and explains the SSM prerequisites (running SSM Agent, instance profile with `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore`, and VPC interface endpoints `ssm`, `ssmmessages`, `ec2messages` or NAT).

Lists the EC2 target prerequisites for SSM fault injection: running SSM Agent, `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` on the instance profile, and network reachability to `ssm`, `ssmmessages`, and `ec2messages` endpoints
Includes `ssm:SendCommand`, `ssm:CancelCommand`, and `ssm:ListCommands` permissions on the `FISExperimentRole`

evals.prompt: Design a multi-action AWS FIS experiment template that simulates a full Single-AZ power/availability loss in `ap-south-1a` across EC2 Auto Scaling instances (`aws:ec2:stop-instances`), ECS tasks (`aws:ecs:stop-task`), and subnet network blackholing (`aws:network:disrupt-connectivity`), sequencing the actions with `startAfter` and verifying recovery with a composite CloudWatch stop condition.
evals.expected_output: Provides a multi-action FIS experiment template targeting `ap-south-1a` across EC2, ECS, and VPC subnets (`aws:network:disrupt-connectivity` with `scope: all` or `availability-zone`), sequences actions using `startAfter`, and attaches a CloudWatch composite/SLO alarm in `stopConditions`.
expectations: Includes targets and actions scoped to a single Availability Zone (`ap-south-1a`) across compute (`aws:ec2:stop-instances` / `aws:ecs:stop-task`) and network (`aws:network:disrupt-connectivity`)
Chains action execution order using the `startAfter` array property
Binds a CloudWatch alarm (`source: "aws:cloudwatch:alarm"`) in `stopConditions` to automatically roll back network/instance disruptions if cross-AZ failover breaches the SLO

evals.prompt: How do AWS FIS multi-account experiments work when orchestrating fault injection from a central resilience account (`111122223333`) against target resources in member workload accounts (`444455556666` and `777788889999`), and what `experimentOptions` and target account configurations are required?

evals.prompt: Generate a production AWS FIS experiment template that terminates 100% (`ALL`) of our production RDS and EKS instances in `ap-south-1` with `"stopConditions": [{"source": "none"}]` so the experiment never aborts early.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to design a production FIS template with `stopConditions: [{"source": "none"}]` or unbounded `ALL` blast-radius destruction without a stop condition, explains the mandatory safety guardrail requiring a real CloudWatch alarm (`source: "aws:cloudwatch:alarm"`) and bounded blast radius (`COUNT(1)` or `PERCENT(n)` with tag scoping), and provides a safe bounded template.
expectations: Explicitly refuses or warns against using `"stopConditions": [{"source": "none"}]` for a production chaos experiment
Requires binding at least one real CloudWatch alarm (`"source": "aws:cloudwatch:alarm"`) as an automated circuit-breaker stop condition
Recommends bounding the blast radius with tag filters (`ChaosReady=true`), single-AZ scoping, and `COUNT(1)` or conservative `PERCENT(n)` instead of `ALL` across production
